quotes.text: Someone on my team told me I needed to be more 'relatable' online. So now I have an Instagram. I posted a picture of a spreadsheet and apparently that is not what they meant.
quotes.speaker: Pete Buttigieg
quotes.context: Appearance on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, CBS, January 2022
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Buttigieg's whole public persona is the earnest policy-nerd who's slightly out of step with normal human spontaneity, and he leans into that self-image freely. The tell is that his actual social media is quite polished and managed; the self-deprecation is a little too neat for someone who clearly does understand the internet.

quotes.text: I've now been in 57 states? I think one left to go.
quotes.speaker: Barack Obama
quotes.context: Then a Democratic U.S. Senator from Illinois campaigning for president, Obama misspoke at a May 9, 2008 event in Beaverton, Oregon, after a long stretch of travel (he meant 47).

quotes.text: I have now given this exact explanation of how a continuing resolution works to, at a rough count, four hundred journalists. I am available to give it four hundred more times.
quotes.speaker: Susan Collins
quotes.context: Gaggle with reporters in the Senate hallway, covered by Roll Call, October 2023
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Collins is known for patient, almost professorial explanations of Senate procedure and for staying accessible to press even on exhausting topics. The number is the subtle tell; Collins would give a figure like that only in genuine exasperation, and her public composure rarely cracks that far.

quotes.text: People ask why I keep talking about infrastructure. I say, have you driven on I-95 lately? That road is making the argument for me every single day.
quotes.speaker: Joe Biden
quotes.context: Remarks to union workers at a Teamsters Local 107 event in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, October 2021
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Biden's infrastructure obsession is thoroughly documented and he constantly grounds national policy in specific, concrete, working-class imagery. I chose I-95 because it's genuinely one of the most notorious corridors in the country and runs through his beloved Delaware, but he never quite said it this crisply.

quotes.text: In Alberta we have a saying: if you don't like the energy policy, wait five years and there'll be a new government with the exact same energy policy.
quotes.speaker: Jason Kenney
quotes.context: Interview on Power & Politics with Vassy Kapelos, CBC News Network, November 2019
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Kenney is a conservative policy lifer who speaks constantly about Western Canadian resource politics and can be dryly self-aware about regional political cycles. The tell is that he'd rarely joke at the expense of his own policy continuity; he's more likely to frame it as vindication than irony.
